stem: Upper inflorescences show more advanced glandular-trichome maturation than lower inflorescences on the same plant. What is the best assessment approach?
choices: Sample multiple representative canopy positions instead of treating the upper flower as the whole-plant maturity state
Use only the most advanced upper sample
Assume every flower on the plant matures synchronously
Ignore trichome observations and use calendar week only
rationale: Trichome development and maturation can vary with plant age, genotype, and position, so representative sampling across the plant provides a stronger maturity assessment.
